events.title: Canonicalization of Tanakh
events.description: Throughout this era the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible) is gradually canonized. Jewish religious works that were written after the time of Ezra were not canonized, although many became popular among many groups of Jews. Those works that made it into the Greek translation of the Bible (the Septuagint) became known as the deuterocanonical books.

events.title: Christianity splits from Judaism
events.description: Christianity emerges as a movement, and then splits from Judaism.

events.title: Destruction of Second Temple
events.description: The Great Jewish Revolt ended with destruction of the Second Temple and the fall of Jerusalem.

events.title: Period of the Tannaim
events.description: Period of the tannaim, rabbis who organized and debated the Jewish oral law. The decisions of the tannaim are contained in the Mishnah, Beraita, Tosefta, and various Midrash compilations. (see Torah (at Shamash))

events.title: Fall of Masada
events.description: The fall of Masada.

events.title: Jerusalem renamed to Aelia Capitolina
events.description: The Roman emperor Hadrian renamed Jerusalem into Aelia Capitolina and forbade Jews to set foot there.

events.title: Bar Kokhba's revolt against Rome
events.description: Bar Kokhba (Bar Kosiba) leads a doomed Jewish revolt against Rome in response to Hadrian's actions. In the aftermath of the revolt, Hadrian renamed the province of Judea as Syria Palaestina.

events.title: Standardization of Jewish oral law
events.description: The Mishnah, the standardization of the Jewish oral law as it stands today, is redacted by Judah haNasi.

events.title: Period of the Amoraim
events.description: Period of the amoraim, the rabbis of the Talmud.

events.title: Constantine I enacts new restrictive legislature
events.description: Roman Emperor Constantine I enacts new restrictive legislature. Conversion of Christians to Judaism is outlawed, congregations for religious services are curtailed, but Jews are also allowed to enter Jerusalem on the anniversary of the Temple's destruction.

events.title: Julian allows Jews to rebuild Temple
events.description: The last pagan Roman Emperor, Julian, allows the Jews to return to "holy Jerusalem which you have for many years longed to see rebuilt" and to rebuild the Temple.

events.title: Redaction of the Talmud Yerushalmi
events.description: Redaction of Talmud Yerushalmi (Talmud of the land of Israel)

events.title: Main redaction of Talmud Bavli
events.description: The main redaction of Talmud Bavli (Babylonian Talmud) is completed under Rabbis Ravina and Ashi. To a lesser degree, the text continues to be modifed for the next 200 years.

events.title: Period of the Savoraim
events.description: Period the savoraim, the sages in Persia who put the Talmud in its final form. Jews at this time in Israel were living under the oppressive rule of the Byzantines under whom there were two more Jewish revolts and three Samaritan revolts.

events.title: Khazar kingdom founded
events.description: The Khazars (a Turkic semi-nomadic people from Central Asia whose King and members of the upper class adopted Judaism) founded the independent Khazar kingdom in the southeastern part of today's Europe.

events.title: Birth of Islam
events.description: Birth of Islam, which, although among largely pagan Arabs, is influenced by Judaism and Christianity.

events.title: Period of the Gaonim
events.description: Period of the Gaonim (the Gaonic era). Jews in southern Europe and Asia Minor lived under the often intolerant rule of Christian Kings and clerics. Most Jews lived in the Muslim Arab realm (Andalusia, North Africa, Palestine, Iraq and Yemen). Despite sporadic periods of persecution, Jewish communal and cultural life flowered in this period. The universally recognized centers of Jewish life were in Jerusalem and Tiberias (Syria), Sura and Pumbeditha (Iraq). The heads of these law schools were the Gaonim, who were consulted on matters of law by Jews throughout the world.

events.title: Muslim armies invade Spain
events.description: Muslim armies invade and occupy most of Spain (At this time Jews made up about 8% of Spain's population). Under Christian rule, Jews had been subject to frequent and intense persecution, but this was alleviated under Muslim rule. Some mark this as the beginning of the Golden age of Jewish culture in Spain.

links.label: Golden age of Jewish culture in Spain

events.title: Karaites split from rabbinic Judaism
events.description: The Karaites reject the authority of the oral law, and split off from rabbinic Judaism.

events.title: Earliest dated document of Cairo Geniza
events.description: An incomplete marriage contract dated to October 6 of this year is the earliest dated document found in the papers of the Cairo Geniza.

events.title: Golden age of Jewish culture in Spain
events.description: The Golden age of Jewish culture in Spain. Abd-ar-Rahman III becomes Caliph of Spain in 912, ushering in the height of tolerance. Muslims granted Jews and Christians exemptions from military service, the right to their own courts of law, and a guarantee of safety of their property. Jewish poets, scholars, scientists, statesmen and philosophers flourished in and were an integral part of the extensive Arab civilization. This ended with the invasion of Almoravides in 1090.

links.label: Golden age of Jewish culture in Spain

events.title: Saadia Gaon compiles Siddur
events.description: In Iraq, Saadia Gaon compiles his siddur (Jewish prayer book.)

events.title: Rabbi Yitchaki Alfassi writes Rif
events.description: Rabbi Yitchaki Alfassi (from Morocco, later Spain) writes the Rif, an important work of Jewish law.

events.title: Rabbi Shlomo Yitzhaki commentaries on Tanakh
events.description: Rabbi Shlomo Yitzhaki (Rashi) writes important commentaries on almost the entire Tanakh (Hebrew Bible) and Talmud.

events.title: Christian Crusades begin
events.description: Christian Crusades begin, sparking warfare with Islam in Palestine. Crusaders temporarily capture Jerusalem in 1099. Tens of thousands of Jews are killed by European crusaders throughout Europe and in the Middle East.

events.title: Time of the Tosafot
events.description: Time of the tosafot, Talmudic commentators who carried on Rashi's work. They include some of his descendants.

events.title: Moroccan Jews expelled who do not convert
events.description: Moroccan Almoravid ruler Yoseph Ibn Tashfin expels Moroccan Jews who do not convert.

events.title: Maimonides writes Mishneh Torah
events.description: Rabbi Moses ben Maimon, aka Maimonides is the leading rabbi of Sephardic Jewry. Among his many accomplishments, he writes an influential code of law (The Mishneh Torah) as well as, in Arabic, the most influential philosophical work (Guide for the Perplexed) in Jewish history.

events.title: Moses de Leon of Spain
events.description: The life of Moses de Leon, of Spain. He authors the Zohar (Book of Splendor) which contains mystical interpretations of the Torah. This begins the modern form of Kabbalah (esoteric Jewish mysticism).

events.title: Period of the Rishonim
events.description: Period of the Rishonim, the medieval rabbinic sages. Most Jews at this time lived in lands bordering the Mediterranean Sea or in Western Europe under feudal systems. With the decline of Muslim and Jewish centers of power in Iraq, there was no single place in the world which was a recognized authority for deciding matters of Jewish law and practice. Consequently, the rabbis recognized the need for writing commentaries on the Torah and Talmud and for writing law codes that would allow Jews anywhere in the world to be able to continue living in the Jewish tradition.

events.title: Rabbi Jacob ben Asher writes Arba'ah Turim
events.description: Rabbi Jacob ben Asher of Spain writes the Arba'ah Turim (Four Rows of Jewish Law).

events.title: Jews expelled from England by Edward I
events.description: Jews are expelled from England by Edward I by the Statute of Jewry.

events.title: Rabbi Levi ben Gershom
events.description: Rabbi Levi ben Gershom, aka Gersonides. A 14th century French Jewish philosopher best known for his Sefer Milhamot Adonai ("The Book of the Wars of the Lord") as well as for his philosophical commentaries.

events.title: Jews repeatedly expelled from France
events.description: Jews are repeatedly expelled from France and readmitted, for a price.

events.title: Jews invited to Poland
events.description: Persecuted in Western Europe, Jews are invited to Poland by Casimir the Great.

events.title: First Jewish prayer book published
events.description: First Jewish prayer book published in Italy.

events.title: Rabbi Yosef Karo compiles Beit Yosef, Shulkhan Arukh
events.description: Rabbi Yosef Karo spends 20 years compiling the Beit Yosef, an enormous guide to Jewish law. He then writes a more concise guide, the Shulkhan Arukh, that becomes the standard law guide for the next 400 years.

events.title: Jews expelled from Spain, Portugal, Germany
events.description: Approximately 200,000 Jews are expelled from Spain, in 1496 from Portugal and from many German cities. The expelled Jews relocate to the Netherlands, Turkey, Arab lands, and Judea; some eventually go to South and Central America. However, most emigrate to Poland. In later centuries, more than 50% of Jewish world population lived in Poland.

events.title: Jews expelled from Sicily
events.description: Jews expelled from Sicily. As many as 137,000 exiled.

events.title: Jews readmitted to Grand Duchy of Lithuania
events.description: King Alexander of Poland readmits Jews to Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

events.title: Ghetto of Venice established
events.description: Ghetto of Venice established, the first Jewish ghetto in Europe. Many others follow.

events.title: Rabbi Moshe Isserles writes Mappah
events.description: Rabbi Moshe Isserles (The Rama) of Cracow writes an extensive gloss to the Shulkhan Arukh called the Mappah, extending its application to Ashkenazi Jewry.

events.title: King of Poland abolishes special clothes law
events.description: King Sigismund I of Poland abolishes the law that required Jews to wear special clothes.

events.title: First Yiddish book published
events.description: First Yiddish book published, in Poland.

events.title: Issac Luria develops Kabbalah
events.description: Issac Luria develops the modern form of esoteric Jewish mysticism AKA Kabbalah.

events.title: First Hebrew Jewish print house in Lublin
events.description: First Hebrew Jewish printing house in Lublin. 1580-1764.

events.title: First Jewish university
events.description: First Jewish university Jeshiva was founded in Poland.

events.title: First session of Council of Four Lands
events.description: First session of the Council of Four Lands (Va'ad Arba' Aratzot) in Lublin, Poland. 70 delegates from local Jewish kehillot meet to discuss taxation and other issues important to the Jewish community.

events.title: First time separate Jewish Sejm
events.description: First time separate (Va'ad) Jewish Sejm for Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

events.title: False Messiah Sabbatai Zevi
events.description: False Messiah Sabbatai Zevi.

events.title: Jews allowed to forbid Christians into their city
events.description: Jews of Poznan granted a privilege of forbidding Christians to enter into their city.

events.title: Worldwide population of Jewry 750,000
events.description: Jewish population of Poland reached 450,000 or 4.5% whole population. Bohemia 40,000 and Moravia 25,000. Worldwide population of Jewry is estmated at 750,000.

events.title: Massacre of Polish gentry and Jewry
events.description: The Ukrainian Cossack Bohdan Chmielnicki leads a massacre of Polish gentry and Jewry that leaves an estimated 65,000 Jews dead and a similar number of gentry. The total decrease in the number of Jews is estmated at 100,000. [1]

events.title: Jews readmitted to England
events.description: Jews readmitted to England by Oliver Cromwell.

events.title: Israel ben Eliezer founds Hasidic Judaism
events.description: Israel ben Eliezer, known as the Ba'al Shem Tov, founds Hasidic Judaism, a way to approach God through meditation and fervent joy. He and his disciples attract many followers, and establish numerous Hassidic sects. The European Jewish opponents of Hassidim (known as Mitnagdim) argue that one should follow a more scholarly approach to Judaism. Some of the more well known Hassidic sects include Breslover, Lubavitch (Chabad), Satmar, Gerer, and Bobover Hasidim.

events.title: Rabbi Yehuda Hehasi moves to Eretz Yisrael
events.description: Rabbi Yehuda Hehasid moves to Eretz Yisrael accompanied by hundreds of his followers. In preparation for their arrival, the residents of Jerusalem build dwellings and a synagogue. A few days after his arrival, Rabbi Yehuda dies suddenly, to the dismay of his followers.

events.title: Rabbi Yehuda Hehasid's synagogue destroyed
events.description: Arab residents of Jerusalem break into the synagogue built for Rabbi Yehuda Hehasid, destroying it and expelling all Ashkenazy Jews from the city. The attack results from a debt the Ashkenazi community owed the Arab residents from the time of Rabbi Yehuda Hehasid.

events.title: Rabbi Elijah of Vilna
events.description: Rabbi Elijah of Vilna, the Vilna Gaon.

events.title: Moses Mendelssohn and Haskalah movement
events.description: Moses Mendelssohn, and the Haskalah (Enlightenment) movement. He strove to bring an end to the isolation of the Jews so that they would be able to embrace the culture of the Western world, and in turn be embraced by gentiles as equals. The Haskalah opened the door for the development of all the modern Jewish denominations and the revival of Hebrew as a spoken language, but it also paved the way for many who, wishing to be fully accepted into Christian society, converted to Christianity or chose to assimilate to emulate it.

events.title: Rabbi Haim Abulafia invited to Holy Land
events.description: Ottoman authorities invite Rabbi Haim Abulafia (1660-1744), renowned Kabbalist and Rabbi of Izmir, to come to the Holy Land. Rabbi Abulafia is to rebuild the city of Tiberias, which has lain desolate for some 70 years. The city's revival is seen by many as a sign of the coming of the Messiah. (Morgenstern, Arie. "Dispersion and Longing for Zion, 1240-1840". Azure. [2])

events.title: Thousands moved to Eretz Yisrael
events.description: Thousands immigrate to Eretz Yisrael under the influence of Messianic predictions. The large immigration greatly increases the size and strength of the Jewish Settlement in Eretz Yisrael. (Morgenstern, Arie. "Dispersion and Longing for Zion, 1240-1840". Azure. [3])

events.title: Rabbi Agraham Gershon 1st immigrant of Hassidic Aliyah
events.description: Rabbi Abraham Gershon of Kitob (d. 1760) is the first immigrant of the Hassidic Aliyah. He is a respected Talmudic scholar, mystic, and brother-in-law of Rabbi Israel Baal Shem Tov (founder of the Hassidic movement). Rabbi Abraham first settles in Hebron. Later, he relocates to Jerusalem at the behest of its residents. (Encyclopedia Judaica, vol. 9, pp. 514. Gershon of Kitov)

events.title: 1,250,000 Jews worldwide, 750,000 in Poland
events.description: Jewish population of Poland reaches 750,000 or 8.0% of total. The worldwide Jewish population is estimated at 1,200,000.

events.title: Jacob Frank's followers joined ranks of Polish szlachta
events.description: Followers of Jacob Frank joined ranks of Polish szlachta (gentry) of Jewish origins.

events.title: Partitions of Poland
events.description: Partitions of Poland between Russia, Kingdom of Prussia and Austria. Main bulk of World Jewry lives now in those 3 countries. Old privileges of Jewish communities are denounced.

events.title: American Revolution religious freedom guaranteed
events.description: American Revolution; religious Freedom guaranteed. [4], [5]

events.title: French revolution grants full right to Jews
events.description: The French revolution. In 1791 France grants full right to Jews and allows them to become citizens, under certain conditions. [6]

events.title: George Washington letter to Jews in Rhode Island
events.description: In the USA, President George Washington sends a letter to the Jewish community in Rhode Island. He writes that he envisions a country "which gives bigotry no sanction...persecution no assistance". Despite the fact that the US was a predominantly Protestant country, theoretically Jews are given full rights. In addition, the mentality of Jewish immigrants shaped by their role as merchants in Eastern Europe meant they were well-prepared to compete in American society. So far, their number is limited.

events.title: Russian creates Pale of Settlement
events.description: Russia creates the Pale of Settlement that includes land acquired from Poland with a huge Jewish population and in the same year Crimea. The Jewish population of the Pale was 750,000. 450,000 Jews lived in the Prussian and Austrian parts of Poland. [7]

events.title: Napoleon prepared to make Palestine independent Jewish state
events.description: While French troops were in Palestine besieging the city of Acre, Napoleon prepared a Proclamation making Palestine an independent Jewish state, but his unsuccessful attempt to capture Acre prevented it from being issued.

events.title: Golden age of Yiddish literature
events.description: The Golden Age of Yiddish literature, the revivial of Hebrew as a spoken language, and the revival of Hebrew literature. [8]

events.title: Development of Orthodox Judaism
events.description: The development of Orthodox Judaism, a set of traditionalist movements that resisted the influences of modernization that arose in response to the European emancipation and Enlightenment movements; characterized by continued strict adherence to Halakha.

events.title: Greece grants citizenship to Jews
events.description: Greece grants citizenship to Jews.

events.title: Jews help defend Warsaw against Russians
events.description: Jewish militias take part in the defence of Warsaw against Russians.

events.title: Moses Haim Montefiore knighted by Queen Victoria
events.description: Moses Haim Montefiore is knighted by Queen Victoria, the first Jew to receive an English Knighthood.

events.title: Rabbi Yisroel Meir ha-Kohen writes Mishnah Berurah
events.description: Rabbi Yisroel Meir ha-Kohen (Chofetz Chaim) opens an important yeshiva. He writes an authoritative Halakhic work, Mishnah Berurah.

events.title: Classical Reform Judaism begins
events.description: Beginning of the rise of classical Reform Judaism.

events.title: Rabbi Israel Salanter develops Mussar Movement
events.description: Rabbi Israel Salanter develops the Mussar Movement. While teaching that Jewish law is binding, he dismisses current philosophical debate and advocates the ethical teachings as the essence of Judaism.

events.title: Positive-Historial Judaism developed
events.description: Positive-Historical Judaism, later known as Conservative Judaism, is developed.

events.title: First Jew elected to US Congress
events.description: David Levy Yulee of Florida is elected to the United States Senate, becoming the first Jew elected to Congress.

events.title: Norway allows Jews to enter
events.description: Norway allows Jews to enter the country. They are not emancipated until 1891.

events.title: Jews emancipated in England
events.description: Jews emancipated in England.

events.title: Alliance Israelite Universelle founded
events.description: Alliance Israelite Universelle, an international Jewish organization is founded in Paris with the goal to protect Jewish rights as citizens.

events.title: Jews take part in Polish national movement
events.description: Jews are taking active part in Polish national movement, that was followed by January rising.

events.title: Henrietta Szold
events.description: Henrietta Szold: educator, author, social worker and founder of Hadassah.

events.title: Zion Society formed in Frankfurt am Main
events.description: The Zion Society is formed in Frankfurt am Main, Germany.

events.title: Jews given equal rights in Poland
events.description: Jews are given equal rights in Poland. The privileges of some towns regarding prohibition of Jewish settlement are revoked.

events.title: Jews emancipated in Hungary
events.description: Jews emancipated in Hungary.

events.title: Benjamin Disraeli becomes Prime Minister of UK
events.description: Benjamin Disraeli becomes Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. Though converted to Christianity as a child, he is the first person of Jewish descent to become a head of state in Europe.

events.title: Russian Zionists set up Jewish settlements
events.description: Russian Zionist group Hovevei Zion (Lovers of Zion) and Bilu (est. 1882) set up a series of Jewish settlements in the Land of Israel, financially aided by Baron Edmond James de Rothschild. In Rishon LeZion Eliezer ben Yehuda revives Hebrew as spoken modern language.

events.title: Jews emancipated in Italy
events.description: Jews emancipated in Italy.

events.title: Jews emancipated in Germany
events.description: Jews emancipated in Germany.

events.title: Reform Judaism founded in Cincinati
events.description: Reform Judaism's Hebrew Union College is founded in Cincinnati. Its founder was Rabbi Isaac Mayer Wise, the architect of American Reform Judaism. Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion

links.label: Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion

events.title: New Hampshire last to give Jews equal political rights
events.description: New Hampshire becomes the last state to give Jews equal political rights.

events.title: 7.7 million Jews worldwide
events.description: World Jewish population around 7.7 million, 90% in Europe, mostly Eastern Europe; around 3.5 million in the former Polish provinces.

events.title: First wave of Pogroms
events.description: Three major waves of pogroms kill tens of thousands of Jews in Russia and Ukraine. More than two million Jews emigrate in the period 1881-1920.

events.title: Second wave of Pogroms
events.description: Three major waves of pogroms kill tens of thousands of Jews in Russia and Ukraine. More than two million Jews emigrate in the period 1881-1920.

events.title: Third wave of Pogroms
events.description: Three major waves of pogroms kill tens of thousands of Jews in Russia and Ukraine. More than two million Jews emigrate in the period 1881-1920.

events.title: First Aliyah
events.description: The First Aliyah, a major wave of Jewish immigrants to build a homeland in Palestine. Aliyah

events.title: Jewish Theological Seminary established
events.description: Rabbi Sabato Morais and Alexander Kohut begin to champion the Conservative Jewish reaction to American Reform, and establish The Jewish Theological Seminary of America as a school of 'enlightened Orthodoxy'.

events.title: 'Zionism' coined
events.description: The term "Zionism" is coined by an Austrian Jewish publicist Nathan Birnbaum in his journal Self Emancipation and was defined as the national movement for the return of the Jewish people to their homeland and the resumption of Jewish sovereignty in the Land of Israel. The book Protocols of the Elders Of Zion written in Russia falsely depicting Jewish atrocities. Proven false, yet still printed and cited today by anti zionist groups. Initially accepted as true by both Hitler and Henry Ford.

events.title: Theodore Herzl writes Der Judenstaat
events.description: In response to the Dreyfus affair, Theodore Herzl writes Der Judenstaat (The Jewish State), advocating the creation of a free and independent Jewish state in Israel.

events.title: The Bund formed in Russia
events.description: The Bund is formed in Russia.

events.title: First Russian Empire Census
events.description: First Russian Empire Census: 5,200,000 of Jews, 4,900,000 in the Pale. The Kingdom of Poland has 1,300,000 Jews or 14% of population.

events.title: Jewish Theological Seminary reorganized, made institution of Conservative Judaism
events.description: Rabbi Dr. Solomon Schechter reorganizes the Jewish Theological Seminary and makes it into the flagship institution of Conservative Judaism.

events.title: Rabbi Abraham Joshua Heschel
events.description: Rabbi Abraham Joshua Heschel, one of the most significant Jewish theologian of the twentieth century.

events.title: Yeshiva College established in New York
events.description: Yeshiva College (later University) and its Rabbi Issac Elchanan Rabbinical Seminary is established in New York for training in a Modern Orthodox milieu.

events.title: British gain control of land of Israel
events.description: The British defeat the Turks and gain control of the land of Israel. The British issue the Balfour Declaration 1917 which gives official British support for "the establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people". Many Jews interpret this to mean that all of Palestine was to become a Jewish controlled state.

events.title: Pale of Settlement abolished
events.description: The Pale of Settlement is abolished, and Jews get equal rights.

events.title: Golden age of hazzanut
events.description: The period between the two World Wars is often referred to as the "golden age" of hazzanut (cantors). Some of the great Jewish cantors of this era include Abraham Davis, Moshe Koussevitzky, Zavel Kwartin (1874-1953), Jan Peerce, Joseph Yossele Rosenblatt (1880-1933), Gershon Sirota (1874-1943), and Laibale Waldman.

events.title: British Mandate of Palestine
events.description: At the San Remo conference Britain receives the League of Nations' British Mandate of Palestine.

events.title: British military admin. of Mandate replaced by civilian rule
events.description: British military administration of the Mandate is replaced by civilian rule.

events.title: Palestine east of Jordan closed to Jews
events.description: Britain proclaims that all of Palestine east of the Jordan River is forever closed to Jewish settlement, but not to Arab settlement.

events.title: Polish-Soviet peace treaty in Riga
events.description: Polish-Soviet peace treaty in Riga. Citizens of both sides are given rights to choose the country. Hundred thousands of Jews, especially small businesses forbidden in the Soviets, move to Poland.

events.title: Jewish Institute of Religion established
events.description: Reform Rabbi Stephen S. Wise established the Jewish Institute of Religion in New York. (It merged with Hebrew Union College in 1950.)

events.title: Britain gives Golan Heights to French Mandate of Syria
events.description: Britain gives the Golan Heights to the French Mandate of Syria. Arab immigration is allowed; Jewish immigration is not.

events.title: 2,989,000 Jews in Poland
events.description: 2,989,000 Jews according to religion poll in Poland (10,5% of total). Jewish youth consisted 23% of students of high schools and 26% of students of universities.

events.title: Kesser Torah yeshivot founded in Poland
events.description: Generally, prior to World War I, there were no chassidic yeshivot in Europe, but on Lag Ba'Omer 1926, the Rabbi Shlomo Chanoch Hacohen Rabinowicz, the fourth Radomsker Rebbe [9] said, "The time has come to found yeshivos where the younger generation will be able to learn and toil in Torah.", leading to the founding of the "Kesser Torah" yeshivot throughout Poland.

events.title: World Jewry: 15,000,000
events.description: World Jewry: 15,000,000. Main countries USA(4,000,000), Poland (3,500,000 11% of total), Soviet Union (2,700,000 2% of total), Romania (1,000,000 6% of total). Palestine 175,000 or 17% of total 1,036,000.

events.title: Hitler takes over Germany
events.description: Hitler takes over Germany; his anti-Semitic sentiments are well-known, prompting numerous Jews to emigrate.

events.title: Adin Steinsaltz born
events.description: Adin Steinsaltz born, author of the first comprehensive Babylonian Talmud commentary since Rashi in the 11th century.

events.title: Britain issues White Paper, reverses support of Balfour Declaration
events.description: The British government issues the 'White Paper' and reverses their support of the Balfour Declaration. They announce an absolute limit of only 75,000 on future Jewish immigration to Palestine.

events.title: The Holocaust
events.description: The Holocaust (Ha Shoah).

events.title: Post-Holocaust refugee crisis
events.description: Post-Holocaust refugee crisis. British detain many Jews making aliyah to Palestine in detention camps.

events.title: Jewish underground movements
events.description: The struggle for the creation of a Jewish state in the British mandate of Palestine is resumed by Jewish underground movements: Haganah, Irgun, and Lehi (group).

events.title: UN approves creation of Jewish State
events.description: The United Nations approves the creation of a Jewish State and an Arab state in the British mandate of Palestine.

events.title: State of Israel declares independent
events.description: The State of Israel declares itself as an independent nation. Andrei Gromyko, the Soviet Union's UN ambassador, calls for the UN to accept Israel as a member state. The UN approves.

events.title: Arab-Israeli War
events.description: 1948 Arab-Israeli War: Syria, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon and Egypt invade Israel. The attack fails. See also 1949 Armistice Agreements and Immigration to Israel from Arab lands.

events.title: 250,000 Holocaust survivors to Israel
events.description: Almost 250,000 Holocaust survivors make their way to Israel. "Operation Magic Carpet" brings thousands of Yemenite Jews to Israel.

events.title: Egypt's president calls for destruction of Israel
events.description: The 1956 Suez War Egypt blockades the Gulf of Aqaba, and closes the Suez canal to Israeli shipping. Egypt's President Nasser calls for the destruction of Israel. Israel, England, and France go to war and force Egypt to end the blockade of Aqaba, and open the canal to all nations.

events.title: Jewish-Christian relations revolutionized by Vatican II
events.description: Jewish-Christian relations are revolutionized by the Catholic Church's Vatican II.

events.title: First Hebrew writer to win Nobel Prize
events.description: Shmuel Yosef Agnon (1888-1970) becomes the first Hebrew writer to win the Nobel Prize in literature.

events.title: Egypt demands UN dismantle UNEF I
events.description: Egyptian President Nasser demands that the UN dismantle the UN Emergency Force I (UNEF I) between Israel and Egypt. The UN complies and the last UN peacekeeper is out of Sinai and Gaza by May 19.

events.title: Egypt declared at war with Israel
events.description: Egyptian PresidentGamal Abdel Nasser closes the strategic Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping and states that Egypt is in a state of war with Israel. Egyptian troops group in the Sinai.

events.title: Six-Day War
events.description: The Six-Day War.

events.title: Three No's of Khartoum
events.description: The Arab Leaders meet in Khartoum, Sudan. The Three No's of Khartoum: No recognition of Israel. No negotiations with Israel. No peace with Israel.

events.title: Reconstructionist Judaism
events.description: Rabbi Mordechai Kaplan formally creates a separate Reconstructionist Judaism movement by setting up the Reconstructionist Rabbinical College in Philadelphia.[10], [11], [12]

events.title: Revival of Klezmer music
events.description: Growing revival of Klezmer music (The folk music of European Jews). [13], [14]

events.title: Yom Kippur War
events.description: The Yom Kippur War. Syria, Egypt and Morocco launch a surprise attack against Israel. Subsequently, OPEC reduces oil production, driving up oil prices and triggering a global economic crisis.

events.title: Jackson-Vanik amendment signed
events.description: President Gerald Ford signs legislation including the Jackson-Vanik amendment, which ties U.S. trade benefits to the Soviet Union to freedom of emigration for Jews.

events.title: UN equates Zionism with racism
events.description: United Nations adopts resolution equating Zionism with racism. Rescinded in 1991.

events.title: Israel rescutes hostages taken to Uganda
events.description: Israel rescues hostages taken to Entebbe, Uganda.

events.title: Israel, Egypt sign peace treaty
events.description: At Camp David, near Washington D.C., Israel and Egypt sign a comprehensive peace treaty, The Camp David Accord, which included the withdrawal of Israel from the Sinai.

events.title: Yiddish writer receives Nobel Prize
events.description: Yiddish writer Isaac Bashevis Singer receives Nobel Prize

events.title: Begin and Sadat awarded Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: Prime Minister Menachem Begin and President Anwar Sadat are awarded Nobel Peace Prize.

events.title: Rescue of Ethiopian Jewry
events.description: Operation Elijah: Rescue of Ethiopian Jewry.

events.title: Lebanon War
events.description: The Lebanon War. Israel invades Southern Lebanon to drive out the PLO.

events.title: American Reform Jews create new definition of Jew
events.description: American Reform Jews formally accept patrilineal descent, creating a new definition of who is a Jew.

events.title: Rescue Ethiopian Jewry by Israel
